page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, providing 128 dedicated vCPUs. Accompanying this processing capacity is 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 36 Gbps without hardware GPU acceleration.

With its high thread count and 2.0 GB per core ratio, ecs.c9i.32xlarge prioritizes parallel computing throughput over memory footprint. The allocation of 128 dedicated cores offers extensive horizontal parallelism for compute-intensive workloads. Because local storage is absent, all persistent storage operations rely entirely on the 36 Gbps network interface, which also multiplexes distributed cluster traffic and external data transfer.

From a resource efficiency perspective, instances configured with a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio minimize expenditure on unused memory capacity in CPU-bound applications. The hardware profile of ecs.c9i.32xlarge fits distributed compute clusters, continuous integration compilation tasks, multi-threaded scientific modeling, and parallel batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. Delivered via the KVM hypervisor, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, representing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 36 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without local disk storage or GPU acceleration. By eliminating excess memory capacity and integrated physical drives, this configuration offers high resource efficiency for environments where CPU execution is the primary operational bottleneck. The instance is suited for parallel workloads such as large-scale batch processing, distributed software compilation, scientific simulations, and compute-bound data pipeline processing.
